lessons.title: Synonym and Antonym
lessons.concept: Synonym = same meaning; Antonym = opposite meaning. Choose the word closest in meaning (or opposite).
lessons.worked_example: Synonym of Abundant = Plentiful. Antonym of Permanent = Temporary.
mistakes: Choosing related but not same word

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension
lessons.concept: Read passage and answer based ONLY on given info. True/False/Can't tell. Don't use outside knowledge.
lessons.worked_example: Statement supported by passage = True; contradicts = False; insufficient info = Can't tell.

lessons.title: Sentence Correction
lessons.concept: Identify grammatical error / choose correct sentence. Subject-verb agreement, tense, articles, prepositions.
lessons.worked_example: She go to school → She goes to school (3rd person singular).

practice.question: Synonym of Abundant?
practice.explanation: Abundant = plentiful, existing in large quantities.

practice.question: Choose the correct sentence.

options.A: Each of the students have submitted the form.
options.B: Each of the students has submitted the form.
options.C: Each of the students are submitting.

practice.explanation: 'Each of + plural noun' takes a singular verb: 'has'. The headword 'Each' is singular regardless of the prepositional phrase after it.

practice.question: Choose the correct word: 'The two candidates were equally _____ for the post.'
practice.explanation: 'Eligible for a post/position' is the fixed collocation for meeting formal qualifications; 'able' requires a to-infinitive (able to work), 'capable of' takes a noun/gerund, and 'intelligent for the post' is not idiomatic.

practice.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.

options.A: The committee are divide in their opinions.
options.B: The committee is divided on the issue.
options.C: The committee is divide on the issue.
options.D: The committee were divide on the issue.

practice.explanation: A collective noun acting as a single unit takes a singular verb ('is'), and 'divided' is the correct past-participle form; the other options use the base form 'divide'.

practice.question: Choose the correct sentence.

options.A: Neither of the answers are correct.
options.B: Neither of the answers is correct.
options.C: Neither of the answer is correct.

practice.explanation: 'Neither of + plural noun' takes a singular verb in standard usage: 'is correct'. 'Neither answers' is ungrammatical.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.

options.A: He is one of the best player in the team.
options.B: He is one of the best players in the team.
options.C: He is one of the best players in the teams.
options.D: He is one of best players in a team.

questions.explanation: 'One of the' requires a plural noun (players) followed by a singular verb on the main subject (is): 'one of the best players in the team'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.

options.A: Hardly he had left when it started raining.
options.B: Hardly had he left when it started raining.
options.C: Hardly he left than it started raining.
options.D: Hardly did he left when it started raining.

questions.explanation: After a negative adverb (hardly, rarely, never, seldom) at the start of a sentence, English uses inversion: 'Hardly had he left when...'. 'Than' pairs with 'no sooner', and 'did he left' misuses the base form.
